equity_bridge.note: Q2 FY2026 balance sheet. Their ~C$2.7m/yr of earnings sit below the EBITDA line used in the flows (matching-asset rule). ~C$63.9m of this is the 50% CCL-Kontur Russian label JV (Analysis JSON), exposed to sanctions/nationalisation; held at book rather than haircut because it is C$0.45/share in total.

equity_bridge.item: Net defined-benefit pension deficit, after tax
equity_bridge.note: FY2025 net pension deficit C$302.8m x (1 - 26%) = C$224.1m. Debt-like claim funded from operating cash beyond the service cost already inside EBITDA; the unlevered flows do not otherwise see it. FY2026 contributions guided at C$95m incl. DC plans.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: base-case mid-horizon organic growth (years 3-5), not the equity CAGR
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 11.4% exceeds revenue 5yr CAGR 7.9% by 44% (>30% threshold). The book-value compounding is inflated by CAD-weakness translation gains in OCI (C$330m in H1 FY2026 alone) and a ~28% dividend payout, not by faster underlying growth; it is rejected as the forward proxy. Revenue CAGRs include acquisitions (~1-2pp/yr) and FX; organic growth has run 3-5%.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs are on the owner-FCF series (reported FCF less SBC): FY2020 586.0, FY2022 507.0, FY2025 822.5. The 3yr owner-FCF CAGR (17.5%) is flattered by the FY2022 working-capital build trough and the FY2025 release; the 5yr 7.0% is the representative figure. Owner-FCF 5yr CAGR (7.0%) sits slightly below reported (7.5%) because SBC grew from 14.1 to 40.7 over the period, i.e. SBC is growing faster than cash flow, though at 0.5% of revenue it is immaterial to value. Periods: FY2020 -> FY2025 (5yr), FY2022 -> FY2025 (3yr), Dec year-end.

scenario_narratives.base: CCL keeps doing what it has done for a decade: 3-4% organic growth in labels and packaging, bolt-on acquisitions funded from cash (not credited here), margins held at the top of the peer range around 21-21.5% adjusted EBITDA. FY2026 lands around +7% with Sleever/ALT and easing comparatives; Avery DTC and CCL Secure banknote/passport wins offset a soft Checkpoint MAS year and memory-chip constraints at CCL Design; the Innovia German thin-gauge line reaches profitability by end-2026 as guided. Capex normalises from the 2024-26 growth programme toward D&A. Terminal growth 2.5% at a Gordon multiple of ~17x owner FCF (below the 18x cap).
scenario_narratives.bull: The 2024-26 capex cycle (RFID inlay Mexico, Bangladesh/Vietnam apparel labelling, EcoFloat shrink film in Poland, coating lines in Mexico/UK, German thin-gauge line) fills faster than planned, lifting organic growth to 5-6% for three years and adjusted EBITDA margin to 22.5% as fixed-cost leverage and the Sleever/Innovia integrations land. Checkpoint RFID expands beyond apparel into non-retail categories, Avery DTC keeps compounding at double digits, and polymer banknote/passport substrate becomes a multi-year volume driver. CAD stays weak, flattering translated results. Terminal growth 3.0%, Gordon capped at 18x.
scenario_narratives.bear: A European/Middle East energy shock and renewed US tariff friction hit volumes in FY2027: organic growth stalls (+0.5%), Innovia cannot pass through resin and energy costs and the German start-up losses persist, Checkpoint's MAS/apparel labelling continues its structural decline faster than RFID replaces it, and CCL Design loses automotive/electronics volume to the memory-chip shortage. Adjusted EBITDA margin compresses to 19.5% (the FY2022 trough level) and does not recover; growth settles at 2%. Leverage stays comfortable (1.0-1.3x), so this is a margin-and-growth bear, not a solvency one; the model does not touch the zero floor.

valuation_philosophy.summary: CCL is valued as a mature, high-quality global packaging compounder: owner FCF (after the small SBC charge) built from a ~21% adjusted-EBITDA margin, 6% D&A, capex converging to D&A, 26% cash tax and working capital that consumes 8% of incremental revenue, discounted at an 8.5% CAD WACC with a 2.5% terminal growth rate. Leases are treated as debt (CCL's own definition) and renewal is charged through capex. No acquisition growth is credited beyond the already-paid-for FY2026 deals, because acquisition cash is likewise excluded from the flows. Buybacks are value-neutral in this model (they fund the flat count); CCL's actual count shrinkage is upside the model does not price.
key_risks_to_valuation: Terminal value carries most of the EV at an 8.5% WACC / 2.5% g; a 1pp WACC move shifts value by roughly 12-15%.
Margin ceiling: CCL already sits at the top of peer margins; the base case assumes they hold, the bear case a reversion to the FY2022 trough.
Checkpoint structural decline (MAS/apparel labelling) outrunning RFID growth; Checkpoint is ~13% of sales.
Energy and resin costs (Innovia, European operations) and the Middle East conflict named in the Q2 FY2026 outlook.
US tariffs and USMCA changes affecting CCL Container and Innovia cross-border flows.
FX translation: 98% of sales outside Canada; a stronger CAD reduces translated revenue, EBITDA and the net-debt-covering cash flows.
Acquisition discipline: M&A is excluded from the flows here, but a large overpaid deal would destroy value the model does not see.
US$500m 3.25% notes due October 2026 refinance at roughly 5%, lifting net finance cost (not in the unlevered flows, but in the WACC's debt leg).
CCL-Kontur: 50% stake in Russian label plants (~C$63.9m carrying value) carried at book in the bridge; sanctions or nationalisation would write it to zero (C$0.37/share).

Roll-up dependence: ~C$3.1bn of goodwill and indefinite-life intangibles; a CGU slowdown triggers non-cash impairments, and growth beyond organic requires continued deal flow the model does not credit.

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API, CCL-B.TO regular close at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 74.69-98.59 CAD; CCL-A.TO parity check same session.
data_sources.financials: CCL-B.TO_Metrics.csv (core_metrics, FY2016-Q2 FY2026, CAD millions); CCL-B.TO_Annual_FY2025.txt (adjusted EBITDA history, tax rate, D&A split incl. ROU depreciation, lease lines, dilutive securities, outlook, 2026 capex guidance); CCL-B.TO_Quarterly_Q2-2026.txt (30 June 2026 balance sheet, net debt table, issued shares, ALT/Sleever acquisitions, Section 13 Outlook).
data_sources.qualitative: CCL-B.TO_Analysis.json (2026-10-10): business model, moat, bull/bear axes, Russian JV and pension-deficit disclosures; company MD&A outlook sections (FY2025 annual, Q2 FY2026 interim). The Analysis landed after the driver paths were set; it confirmed the narratives (RFID, Avery DTC, Secure wins, Innovia ramp, tariffs, start-up overruns, Checkpoint lumpiness) and added the two bridge items.

inputs.share_count_basis: 169.6m Class A + Class B issued and outstanding at 30 June 2026 (Q2 FY2026 MD&A) plus ~1.0m dilutive DSUs/RSUs/PSUs (FY2025 diluted-EPS note: 0.3m DSU + 0.7m share-based) = 170.6m fully diluted. Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows, so charging dilution too would double-count. CCL is a net repurchaser (C$331.6m in H1 FY2026 alone, C$300m in FY2025), so the flat count is more than funded; the model gives no credit for the shrinking count beyond that.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 consolidated cash flow statement, 'Equity-settled share-based payment transactions' C$40.7m (FY2024 C$33.7m). No separate net-share-settlement tax line is disclosed; CCL settles most awards in cash through the equity note, so the cash-flow add-back is the combined figure.
inputs.interest_income_note: FY2025 finance income C$29.8m (C$16.6m interest on cash). NOT stripped: CCL carries net debt of C$1,741.6m (1.05x adjusted EBITDA), so the cash is netted against debt in the bridge and nothing is counted twice. The forward flows are unlevered (built from EBITDA), so neither finance income nor finance cost enters them.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 financing-activity repurchases C$300.0m; H1 FY2026 C$331.6m (Q1 67.5 + Q2 264.1). Actual cash, not authorization.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-09T20:00:00Z regular close (TSX). CCL-A.TO (voting) closed 94.89 the same session, 0.5% above the B shares -- normal dual-class parity.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in CAD, the currency of the statements and flows. Rf ~3.8% (Government of Canada 10y, Oct-2026, judged ~100bp below the 5.2% UST 10y printed by Yahoo ^TNX on 2026-10-09), ERP 5.5%, beta ~0.95 (diversified global packaging/label converter, 98% of sales outside Canada, GDP-plus but cyclical through Checkpoint/Innovia) -> cost of equity ~9.0%. Debt: 3.05% US$ notes 2030, 3.25% US$ notes Oct-2026 (refinancing at ~5%), 3.864% C$ notes 2028, revolver ~5% -> blended pre-tax ~4.5%, after-tax ~3.3% at 26%. Market weights ~90% equity (170.6m x C$94.46 = C$16.1bn) / ~10% debt (C$2.7bn gross). WACC = 0.90 x 9.0 + 0.10 x 3.3 = 8.4%, rounded to 8.5%. Same WACC in all three scenarios: cyclicality, tariffs, Middle East energy and the Checkpoint decline are charged once, in the scenario flows and weights, not in the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (A), leases as debt, matching CCL's own 'Total debt' definition: lease liabilities C$216.2m (51.9 current + 164.3 non-current at 30 June 2026) are inside total_debt/net_debt. Lease principal (FY2025 C$54.2m; H1 FY2026 C$28.2m) and lease interest (FY2025 C$9.1m) are therefore NOT deducted from the flows. Post-IFRS-16 EBITDA is used with D&A INCLUDING right-of-use depreciation (FY2025 C$56.6m of the C$465.2m total) so EBIT for cash tax is right, and ongoing lease-asset renewal is charged through the capex line: capex_pct includes ~0.7pp of revenue (~C$56m/yr) of ROU-asset renewal on top of the ~5.7% guided PP&E spend. Multiples consistency: lease-inclusive EV against post-IFRS-16 adjusted EBITDA.
inputs.nci_treatment: No material non-controlling interest on the balance sheet; flows are 100% attributable. Equity-accounted investments (C$77.1m at 30 June 2026) earn ~C$2.7m/yr BELOW the operating-income line used to build EBITDA, so the income is excluded from the flows and the asset is added to the bridge at book (matching-asset rule). The after-tax net pension deficit is deducted in the bridge as a debt-like item.
inputs.wc_note: Net working capital at 31 Dec 2025: receivables 1,293.4 + inventories 805.0 - payables 1,467.2 = C$631.2m = 8.2% of revenue. Manufacturer: growth consumes cash, so wc_capture_pct is NEGATIVE (-8%) on the change in revenue.
inputs.ebitda_basis: Metrics.csv EBITDA is DERIVED (operating income + total D&A, after restructuring and other items): FY2025 C$1,617.6m = 21.1% of sales. CCL's own Adjusted EBITDA (before restructuring/other, after corporate expense) was C$1,622.5m FY2025, C$1,497.1m FY2024, C$1,332.1m FY2023, C$1,231.4m FY2022, C$1,173.1m FY2021, C$1,123.2m FY2020 (19-21% of sales every year); TTM to June 2026 C$1,664.7m; H1 FY2026 C$865.0m = 21.4% of sales. The margin paths use the derived (post-restructuring) basis, anchored at 21.1-21.2%.
inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF DCF, component route (10-year explicit build, Gordon terminal capped at 18x owner FCF). ROUTING: CCL is a diversified operating company (CCL Segment labels/aluminium containers/secure, Avery, Checkpoint, Innovia films) reporting in CAD on the TSX; non-US, moderately cyclical, IFRS-16 leases -> owner-fcf.md plus the adaptations file (CAD WACC, one lease treatment, matching-asset rule, risk charged once). First valuation of this ticker; no MEMORY.md entry. FY0 = FY2025 (Dec year-end); year 1 of the projection is FY2026, which is three quarters complete at the valuation date: H1 FY2026 sales +6.0% (3.5% organic, 1.1% M&A, 1.4% FX), Q2 +9.1% (5.0% organic, 1.8% M&A from ALT and Sleever acquired in-quarter, 2.3% FX), Q3 orders 'stable', modest FX tailwind guided. Net debt and share count are from the 30 June 2026 interim balance sheet (latest filing); the Sleever (C$148.4m) and ALT (C$29.1m) consideration is already in that net debt, so the FY2026 growth that includes them is paid for. Growth after FY2026 is organic-plus-carryover only: no unfunded M&A is credited in any scenario, matching the exclusion of acquisition cash from the flows. The derived shares_outstanding column in Metrics.csv (net income / diluted EPS, ~170.8m at Q2 FY2026) was replaced by the printed 169.6m issued count plus the FY2025 dilutive-securities effect. Owner FCF anchor: reported FCF 863.2 (OCF 1,304.4 - gross capex 441.2; CCL's own 'free cash flow from operations' nets C$28.1m of disposal proceeds and prints 891.3) less SBC 40.7 = 822.5 (10.7% of sales). Component-built FY2026 owner FCF is ~C$810m (~9.9% of sales): FY2025 benefited from a working-capital release and sub-guidance capex, which the build does not carry forward. SBC is 0.5% of revenue, so house and street bases differ by only a few dollars per share; the band is real but narrow.

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 +7.0%: H1 actual +6.0%, H2 carries a full half of Sleever/ALT (~2.5pp), 4-5% organic with easing comparatives (aluminium container plant back at full capacity, Avery back-to-school ahead of the tariff-hit 2025, CCL Secure banknote/passport wins), and a modest FX tailwind, partly offset by Checkpoint MAS below 2025 and CCL Design memory-chip constraints. FY2027 +4.5% = ~1pp Sleever carryover plus 3.5% organic. Thereafter organic only, 4.0% fading to 2.5% by year 8 -- GDP-plus for labels/packaging with no unfunded M&A credited.
base.margin_rationale: Anchored at 21.2% (FY2025 derived 21.1%, H1 FY2026 21.4% with Sleever initially dilutive). Drifts to 21.5% by year 5 as the German thin-gauge film line turns profitable, Sleever integration completes and the 2024-25 capex (RFID Mexico, Bangladesh/Vietnam, EcoFloat Poland) fills. Capped at 21.5%: CCL already says its margins are 'at the top end of the range of its peers'.
base.capex_rationale: 2026 guided net capex ~C$470m (~5.7% of ~C$8.2bn) plus ~0.7pp ROU-asset renewal under lease treatment (A) = 6.4%, converging to D&A (6.0%) by year 5 as growth slows toward GDP. D&A 6.0% = FY2025 465.2/7,663.8 (6.07%), H1 FY2026 5.98%.
base.tax_rationale: FY2025 effective rate 25.9% on a 25.5% Canadian statutory base; cash taxes paid 300.2 on 1,081.2 pre-tax (27.8%) caught up on prior years, while H1 FY2026 cash tax (102.9) ran below expense (148.1). 26% flat on unlevered EBIT; no NOLs or one-off credits to ramp from.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 18x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Moved from the 15/50/35 house default to 25/50/25. Bear up to 25%: the Q2 FY2026 MD&A itself names a closed Strait of Hormuz, European energy costs and constricted supply chains as the operating backdrop, Checkpoint is guided below 2025 for H2, and Innovia is still carrying start-up losses -- the bear axes are live, not hypothetical, though none threatens solvency at 1.05x leverage. Bull down to 25%: the bull case needs several independent things to go right at once (RFID beyond apparel, Innovia turnaround, Avery DTC, Secure substrate wins, Sleever synergies) and CCL already earns top-of-peer margins, so 22.5% is a stretch, not a reversion. Base 50%: a steady GDP-plus compounder with a 20-year record of exactly this.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
